topics.title: Quick Start
topics.summary: Create, edit, inspect, and save a map.
body: Choose Fueling, Ignition Timing, or Map Sandbox.
Set the matrix size and edit or paste the X and Y axis breakpoints.
Drag across cells to select an area. Hold Ctrl while clicking or dragging to add another area.
Type into a selected cell and press Enter to apply that value to every selected cell. Clicking away cancels a pending group edit.
Smooth the selection and inspect the result in the 3D view.
Save the workspace as a .map file or export the active table to CSV or Excel.

topics.title: How the Tables Relate
topics.summary: Understand which dimensions, axes, values, and histories are shared or independent.
body: Fueling and Ignition Timing keep separate MAP scales and MAP units.
Fueling and Ignition Timing use coordinated matrix dimensions and RPM scaling.
Map Sandbox is independent of both engine maps.
Timing, Fueling, Learn Apply, and Sandbox maintain their own Undo and Redo histories.

topics.title: Map Colors and Heat-Map Scaling
topics.summary: Choose a global palette while scaling each table to its own value range.
body: Open Settings and choose Adjust Map Colors to enable custom low and high colors or return to the default spectrum.
The selected palette is global: Fueling, Ignition Timing, and Map Sandbox use the same palette in their 2D tables, 3D viewers, and Excel exports.

Color normalization is independent for each table. The lowest value in a table receives the low end of the palette, the highest value receives the high end, and intermediate values are positioned proportionally between them.
Changing one table's values can shift that table's color distribution without changing the colors assigned to the other tables.
An already-open 3D viewer refreshes when the global palette changes.
Global map colors are retained by autosave and included in .map workspace files.

topics.title: Display Precision and Stored Values
topics.summary: Control how values look separately from how values are stored.
body: Fueling, Ignition Timing, and Map Sandbox each provide Display Leading, Display Trailing, and Display Zeroes controls.

Display Zeroes selects zero through four minimum decimal places for table, tooltip, 3D, and Excel display text. Display Trailing remains the maximum calculated display precision unless the selected zero padding is higher.

The Display Leading threshold takes priority over Display Trailing and Display Zeroes. With Display Leading set to 3, values below 100 can show the selected decimal precision, while values with three or more leading digits are displayed as rounded whole numbers. This display-only rounding does not alter the actual stored value.
Display controls change only how values appear and never rewrite the underlying table values. Lowering Display precision can hide digits; raising it again reveals the original stored digits.
Pasted values and direct single-cell or selected-group edits are stored as entered and are not rounded by display formatting or autosave. Select or focus a cell to see its underlying value.
Fueling, Timing, and Sandbox smoothing, interpolation, and offsets calculate from the full stored values. Their results are also stored independently of the selected Display precision.
The display format is also used by the 3D value scale, 3D tooltip, and Excel number formatting. Clipboard and CSV data use the underlying stored values.

topics.title: Selecting and Editing Cells
topics.summary: Select rectangles, separated areas, complete tables, and transition rings.
body: Left-drag to select a rectangular area. Ctrl+click or Ctrl+drag adds separated cells or another area.
Click one unselected cell to replace the previous selection. Ctrl+A selects the complete active table.
With several cells selected, edit one selected cell and press Enter to apply the value to every selected cell. Clicking away cancels the pending group edit.
Right-click one solid rectangular selection and choose Select transition ring to select an adjustable-width perimeter band while leaving its center unselected.
Choose Highlight region of interest to retain a red rectangular outline after the normal selection is cleared.
Right-click a selection for Copy, Paste, Offset Selection, Interpolate, smoothing, and clear commands.

Offset Selection uses Numerical mode to add or subtract the entered table units. Percentage of value multiplies every selected cell by 1 plus or minus the entered percentage; for example, increasing 80 by 10% produces 88, while increasing it numerically by 10 produces 90. Offset results retain their underlying precision regardless of the Display settings, and each arrow click applies another offset to the current values.
After pasting a complete table of cells, the selection is cleared.

topics.title: Editing X, RPM, Y, and MAP Axes
topics.summary: Edit, paste, auto-fill, and rescale axis breakpoints.
body: Click an axis breakpoint, enter a value, and press Enter. Breakpoints must remain ordered and unique.
Changing a minimum or maximum endpoint automatically rescales that axis.
Drag across axis values and right-click to Auto-fill or paste breakpoints.
Pasted X, RPM, Y, or MAP values are retained as entered; clicking back into the table commits the pasted scale.
MAP uses whole-number kPa values and one decimal place for PSI.
Fuel MAP changes never alter the Ignition Timing MAP scale, and Timing MAP changes never alter Fueling.
Sandbox X and Y units may be standard, Unitless, or custom. Unit changes relabel a Sandbox axis without converting values.

topics.title: Rows, Columns, and Smooth Selected
topics.summary: Choose the smoothing operation that matches the shape of the selection.
body: Smooth Rows reshapes every selected row between its left and right endpoints. It needs at least three columns and leaves the endpoint columns unchanged.
Smooth Columns reshapes every selected column between its top and bottom endpoints. It needs at least three rows and leaves the endpoint rows unchanged.
Smooth Selected opens Advanced Smoothing and operates on the exact selected cells, including separated Ctrl-selected areas.
Rows and Columns operate across the rectangular selection bounds; use Advanced Smoothing for irregular selections.
Interpolate replaces selected interior values with transitions derived from the selected outer values while preserving the applicable anchors.
All operations create an Undo step in the active table.

topics.title: Advanced Smoothing Algorithms
topics.summary: Blend noise, spikes, edges, potholes, and transitions with selectable algorithms.
body: Standard weighted smoothing — Best general-purpose choice for a noisy or slightly lumpy area. It averages each selected value with nearby selected cells, weighting the current cell and direct neighbors more strongly than diagonals.

Standard weighted scenario — Use it after pasting or hand-editing a broad block whose intended overall shape is already correct but whose cell-to-cell changes are uneven. Start near 40–60% strength with one or two passes.

Constrained surface smoothing — Best for softening an irregular patch while keeping its outside shape controlled. It uses local neighboring values; combine it with Preserve Selection Perimeter when the selected edge must remain an anchor and Prevent Value Overshoot when new peaks or dips are not acceptable.
Constrained surface scenario — Select a rough area that already joins the surrounding map correctly at its boundary, preserve the perimeter, and smooth only the interior roughness.

Shape-preserving interpolation — Best when the selection should follow a continuous ramp or slope between its horizontal and vertical endpoints. It blends toward trends derived from the outer selected values instead of merely averaging local noise.

Shape-preserving scenario — Use it on a diagonal transition, sloped timing ramp, or VE area that should progress steadily between known low and high edges. Preserve the perimeter when those endpoints must not move.

Spike removal (median) — Best for isolated single-cell or small-cluster peaks and pits that are probably editing artifacts. A median-style target rejects an extreme value more strongly than a normal average.

Spike removal scenario — Select an area around one accidental timing spike or VE hole, use moderate strength and one pass, then inspect the result before repeating. Do not use it when the sharp peak or pothole is intentional.

Edge-preserving smoothing — Best for reducing noise without washing across a deliberate step, ridge, plateau, or sharp load transition. Neighbors with values very different from the current cell contribute less.

Edge-preserving scenario — Use it where a boosted region or other intentional feature has a distinct edge but the surfaces on either side are noisy. It is usually safer than general averaging near that edge.

Weighted center / perimeter — Best for reshaping the interior of a broad selection relative to its outside ring. Center Influence controls whether the result is pulled more toward the perimeter average or toward the selection's center average.

Weighted center / perimeter scenario — Use a low Center Influence to blend a raised or lowered interior toward its surrounding boundary; use a higher influence to retain more of a broad center plateau while smoothing its transition to the edge.

Smooth to Surroundings — Best when selected transition cells should blend with nearby unselected cells. The selection is the write area while both selected and fixed surrounding cells participate in the calculation.

Smooth to Surroundings scenario — For an intentional pothole or ridge, select only a transition ring around the feature so the unselected center remains intact. Choose a direction that crosses the wrinkle and increase Neighbor Reach only far enough to sample the stable surrounding surface.

Quick choice — General roughness: Standard Weighted. Anchored interior: Constrained Surface. Predictable ramp: Shape Preserving. Accidental outlier: Spike Removal. Intentional sharp feature: Edge Preserving. Broad center-to-edge contour: Weighted Center / Perimeter. Blend a ring or narrow strip to fixed neighbors: Smooth to Surroundings.
Strength controls how far values move toward the calculated result; Passes repeats the operation. Begin conservatively, inspect the 3D contour, and use Undo before trying a stronger setting.

Preserve Selection Perimeter keeps selected boundary cells fixed. Prevent Value Overshoot restricts results to the starting selected range, or to the sampled neighborhood range when using Smooth to Surroundings.
All smoothing calculations use and retain underlying stored values rather than rounded display text. Display precision does not change smoothing calculations or stored results.

topics.title: Smooth to Surroundings and Transition Rings
topics.summary: Blend a pothole, ridge, or narrow wrinkle without flattening the intended feature.
body: For a pothole or raised feature, select a transition ring and choose Smooth to Surroundings. The unselected center remains a shape anchor.
Only selected cells change; surrounding unselected cells remain fixed references.
Across Columns samples left and right, Across Rows samples above and below, and Both Directions also includes diagonal neighbors.
Neighbor Reach is measured from every selected cell and uses actual X/Y breakpoint spacing when weighting samples.
For a two-cell-wide wrinkle, select only the two rows or columns, start with Reach 2, Strength 50%, and one pass, then inspect the 3D contour.
Use Undo between experiments so each adjustment starts from a known surface.

topics.title: Timing Regions and Boundaries
topics.summary: Divide the timing table into Idle, Cruise, Part Throttle, and WOT operating regions.
body: Choose Set Boundaries, hover over the table, and click the intersecting cell to lock both boundary lines.
The lower-left region is Idle Low MAP and the upper-left region is Idle High MAP.
The lower-right region is Cruise to Part Throttle and the upper-right region is Part Throttle to WOT.
Regional timing profiles can fill regions directly or blend across their boundaries.
Boundary lines are shared visually with Fueling, while each table retains its own values and MAP scale.

topics.title: Boost Timing Offset
topics.summary: Apply a signed timing change per PSI using each selected row's actual MAP breakpoint.
body: Boost Timing Offset is available when the Ignition Timing MAP scale uses PSI gauge.
Select the timing cells to change, enter a signed timing change per PSI, a Low MAP start, and a High MAP maximum.
A negative rate subtracts timing and a positive rate adds timing.

Every selected MAP row is calculated independently from its actual breakpoint: effective boost equals clamp(row PSI, Low MAP, High MAP) minus Low MAP; timing change equals effective boost multiplied by the signed rate.
Nonlinear or irregular PSI breakpoint spacing is respected. The calculation does not assume equal row spacing and does not distribute the total change by row count.
Rows at or below Low MAP receive no change. Rows above High MAP receive the same maximum clamped change.

topics.title: Fueling and VE Setup
topics.summary: Edit raw VE values or generate a starting table with the VE Setup wizard.
body: Fuel cells store editable volumetric-efficiency percentages. View as lb/hr changes only the calculated display.
VE Setup uses engine information and VE targets to create a preview before values are committed.
Forced-induction setup displays MAP inputs in PSI and enables one-, two-, three-bar, or custom MAP sensor selection.
The selected sensor rating proposes an editable maximum boost range. Apply MAP Range rescales only the Fueling MAP breakpoints.
When enabled, final wizard smoothing runs Smooth Columns and Smooth Rows after all contour generation and before preview.
Always review generated values before applying them to an ECU.

topics.title: Learn Apply Table
topics.summary: Paste signed percentage corrections and transfer them to Fueling.
body: Learn Apply holds signed percentage corrections, not absolute VE values. Its dimensions, axes, MAP units, and display precision follow Fueling.
Paste a complete table or select an upper-left destination cell for a partial block. Blank fields leave values unchanged and zero means no correction.
Transfer uses new VE = current VE multiplied by (1 + correction / 100). For example, 80 VE with +10% becomes 88 VE.
Transfer and Smooth Changed Cells applies Smooth to Surroundings after the corrections. Only nonzero correction cells are smoothed.
A transfer and its optional smoothing form one Fueling Undo step. Learn Apply has separate Undo and Redo history.
Learn values autosave with Fueling and are included in .map workspace files.

topics.title: Map Sandbox
topics.summary: Create an independent custom numeric table with configurable axes and units.
body: Use Map Sandbox for custom numeric tables that do not need operating-region boundaries.
Set independent dimensions, breakpoints, and X/Y units. Choose Custom to add or remove unit names.
Sandbox includes selection editing, offsets, smoothing, 3D editing, history, autosave, CSV, and Excel export.
Sandbox changes never modify Fueling or Ignition Timing.

topics.title: 3D Viewing, Selection, and Sculpting
topics.summary: Orbit, inspect, select, edit, and sculpt map surfaces.
body: Right-drag to orbit, use the mouse wheel to zoom, and stationary right-click to open selected-cell tools.
The lower-left orientation widget is a miniature surface using the same values, colors, contours, and rotation.
Open 3D Map with no 2D selection to view the full table, or select one rectangular area of at least two rows by two columns to open a focused workspace.
Hover for the live X/Y/value tooltip and crosshair. Left-click or left-drag selects surface cells; hold Ctrl to add separated cells or areas.
Raise, Lower, Smooth, and Flatten sculpt while left-dragging. Radius follows actual breakpoint spacing and Strength controls blending.
Sculpt changes preview during the drag and commit on mouse-up as one source-table Undo step. Press Escape before mouse-up to cancel.
Clear Selection or Return to Rotation deselects the 3D cells. Closing the viewer clears the corresponding 2D selection.
3D Undo and Redo operate on the viewer's source table.

topics.title: Flatten and Smooth Between Two Points
topics.summary: Edit a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal path while preserving its endpoints.
body: Click the first surface cell and Ctrl+click the second to select two endpoints.
Flatten Path replaces only the interior path cells with a straight value ramp.
Smooth Path softens only the cells along the selected path.
Both endpoints remain unchanged, and horizontal, vertical, and diagonal paths are supported.
Each completed path operation creates one Undo step in the source table.

topics.title: Copy, Paste, CSV, and Excel
topics.summary: Exchange cells and axes with tuning software and spreadsheet files.
body: Copied cells use tab-separated rows and can be moved between Map Lab tables and compatible tuning software.
Select an axis starting point before pasting a copied row or column of breakpoints.
CSV and Excel place the X or RPM scale at the bottom of the table.
Excel includes heat-map conditional formatting matching the application and does not add header filters.

Map Colors in Settings controls one global palette used by the Fueling, Ignition Timing, and Map Sandbox 2D tables, 3D viewers, and Excel exports. Each table independently scales that palette from its own lowest value to its highest value.
Fueling, Ignition Timing, and Map Sandbox each provide their own CSV and Excel export commands.

topics.title: Open, Save, Save As, and Autosave
topics.summary: Save complete Map Lab workspaces in the .map format.
body: Save writes Timing, Fueling, Learn Apply, and Sandbox tables, axes, units, boundaries, colors, display preferences, precision, smoothing choices, and VE options to the current .map file.
The first Save asks for a filename. Save As creates or selects a different .map file.
Open validates the complete file before replacing the current workspaces and makes the opened file the current Save target.
The current filename appears in the application title and every 2D table view. Untitled means no manual Save target has been assigned.
When closing with unsaved changes, choose Yes to save, No to close without updating the file, or Cancel to keep working.
Timing, Fueling, Sandbox, global map colors, and dialog settings autosave for recovery between sessions.

topics.title: Undo, Progress, and Tool Dialogs
topics.summary: Understand independent histories, long operations, and persistent tool windows.
body: Timing, Fueling, Learn Apply, and Sandbox maintain separate Undo and Redo stacks.
Use Undo immediately after an unwanted edit, paste, offset, smoothing operation, resize, or axis change.
Large resizes, smoothing operations, and extensive Undo or Redo changes show a Working progress window.
Only one instance of each modeless tool dialog opens. Selecting its command again restores and activates the existing dialog.
Tool values remain available until changed or the workspace is replaced.

topics.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
topics.summary: Common table-selection, editing, history, and file commands.
body: Ctrl+A — Select every cell in the active table.
Ctrl+C — Copy selected cells.
Ctrl+V — Paste cells or focused axis values.
Ctrl+Z — Undo the active table's last change.
Ctrl+Y — Redo the active table's last undone change.
Ctrl+O — Open a .map workspace.
Ctrl+S — Save the current workspace.
Ctrl+Shift+S — Save As.
F1 — Open Help and focus the search box.
Enter — Commit a cell or axis edit.
Escape — Cancel an interactive boundary selection or an active 3D sculpt preview.

topics.title: Using Help Contents, Index, and Search
topics.summary: Find instructions by category, indexed term, or a full-text search.
body: Contents groups Help topics by feature area. Expand a category and select a topic to read it.
Index lists topic titles and keywords alphabetically. Selecting any index entry opens its associated topic.
Search matches words across titles, summaries, keywords, and instructions. Every entered word must occur in a topic for it to appear in the results.
Press F1 anywhere in Map Lab to open Help and focus the search field.
Use the Clear button or press Escape in the search field to remove the current query.

topics.title: Calibration Safety
topics.summary: Verify generated and edited calibration data before using it on an engine.
body: Map Lab is a calculation, editing, and visualization tool; it does not validate that a calibration is safe for a particular engine.
Verify exported values independently and use appropriate engine safeguards before applying a map to a vehicle.
Keep a known-good calibration backup and make controlled changes while monitoring the engine with suitable instrumentation.
